questions.text: List two elemental semiconductor materials and two compound semiconductor materials.
Sketch three lattice structures: (a) simple cubic, (b) body-centered cubic, and (c) face-centered cubic.
Describe the procedure for finding the volume density of atoms in a crystal.
Describe the procedure for obtaining the Miller indices that describe a plane in a crystal.
Describe the procedure for finding the surface density of atoms on a particular lattice plane.
Describe why a unit cell, that is not a primitive unit cell, might be preferable to a primitive unit cell.
Describe covalent bonding in silicon.
What is meant by a substitutional impurity in a crystal? What is meant by an interstitial impurity?
Determine the number of atoms per unit cell in a (a) face-centered cubic, (b) body-centered cubic, and (c) diamond lattice.
Assume that each atom is a hard sphere with the surface of each atom in contact with the surface of its nearest neighbor. Determine the percentage of total unit cell volume.

Consider a free electron bound within a two-dimensional infinite potential well defined by V = 0 for 0 < x < 40 Å, 0 < y < 20 Å, and V = ∞ elsewhere. (a) Determine the expression for the allowed electron energies. (b) Describe any similarities and any differences with the results of the one-dimensional infinite potential well.

formulas.description: Esta fórmula representa a energia quantizada de uma partícula em uma caixa bidimensional, onde a partícula está restrita a se mover em um espaço com dimensões limitadas. A energia depende dos números quânticos associados às direções x e y, bem como das propriedades físicas do sistema, como a massa da partícula e o tamanho da caixa.

symbols.description: representa a energia da partícula no estado quântico n.
é a constante de Planck, que relaciona a energia de um fóton à frequência da luz.
é uma constante matemática que representa a razão entre a circunferência de um círculo e seu diâmetro.
é a massa da partícula que está se movendo dentro da caixa.
é o comprimento da caixa em que a partícula está confinada.
é o número quântico associado à direção x, que indica o estado quântico da partícula nessa direção.
é o número quântico associado à direção y, que indica o estado quântico da partícula nessa direção.

questions.text: Consider a proton in a one-dimensional infinite potential well. (a) Derive the expression for the allowed energy states of the proton. (b) Calculate the energy difference (in units of eV) between the lowest possible energy and the next higher energy state for (i) a = 1 Å and (ii) a = 0.5 cm.

For the step potential function shown in Figure P2.33, assume that E > V_0 and that particles are incident from the +x direction traveling in the -x direction. (a) Write the wave solutions for each region. (b) Derive expressions for the transmission and reflection coefficients.

Consider an electron with a kinetic energy of 2.8 eV incident on a step potential function of height 3.5 eV. Determine the relative probability of finding the electron at a distance (a) 5 Å beyond the barrier, (b) 15 Å beyond the barrier, and (c) 40 Å beyond the barrier compared with the probability of finding the incident particle at the barrier edge.

(a) Calculate the transmission coefficient of an electron with a kinetic energy of 0.1 eV impinging on a potential barrier of height 1.0 eV and width d = 4 Å (b) Part (a) for a barrier width of 12 Å. (c) Using the results of part (a), determine the density of electrons per second that impinge the barrier if the tunneling current density is 1.2 mA/cm².

(a) Estimate the tunneling probability of a particle with an effective mass of m_{e} = 0.1 m_{0} (an electron in gallium arsenide), where m_{0} is the mass of an electron, tunneling through a rectangular potential barrier of height V_0 = 0.8 eV and width 15 Å. The particle kinetic energy is 0.20 eV. (b) Repeat part (a) if the effective mass of the particle is 1.08m_{0} (an electron in silicon).
Write the equation for charge neutrality for the condition of complete ionization.
Sketch a graph of n_{0} versus temperature for an n-type material.
Sketch graphs of the Fermi energy versus donor impurity concentration and versus temperature.
What is the relevance of the Fermi energy?
